title: Compounding Risk: Sorry-Using Proofs × Production Deployment = Undetected Incomplete Verification

original_idea.body:
# Compounding Risk: Sorry-Using Proofs × Production Deployment = Undetected Incomplete Verification

**Problem:** If Lean 4 proofs using 'sorry' (a placeholder that makes any goal provable) are deployed in production without sorry detection, developers believe they have formal guarantees they do not have. This compounding risk of sorry usage + deployment without sorry checking is not characterized.

**Direction:** Survey open-source Lean 4 code on GitHub. Measure frequency of sorry usage in non-research, non-draft code. Survey developers on whether they check for sorry before deployment. Design and test a simple CI/CD sorry-detection tool. Measure developer awareness of the sorry failure mode.

**Why it matters:** If production Lean 4 code contains sorry placeholders that developers believe are complete proofs, formal verification provides false safety guarantees at scale. This is a practical deployment failure mode that urgently needs characterization.

**Relevant context:** Sorry is documented as a proof debt mechanism in the Lean community. Production sorry usage outside of research is not measured. No CI/CD sorry-detection tool is mentioned in any formal verification deployment paper.
